stories.title: Dunham-Bush Industries Acquires 32 Acres at SPD Tech Valley for RM172 Mil Manufacturing Expansion
stories.summary: Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd will invest approximately RM172 million in the first phase of a new manufacturing facility at SPD Tech Valley in Senawang, Negeri Sembilan, as the heating, ventilation and air conditioning solutions manufacturer seeks to expand its production capacity in Malaysia.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 28): Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd will invest approximately RM172 million in the first phase of a new manufacturing facility at SPD Tech Valley in Senawang, Negeri Sembilan, as the heating, ventilation and air conditioning solutions manufacturer seeks to expand its production capacity in Malaysia.

The company signed a sale and purchase agreement with SPD Tech Valley Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Seri Pajam Development Group (SPD Group), on Friday to acquire approximately 32 acres at the 523-acre freehold industrial park.

Phase 1 is expected to create up to 400 jobs. Construction is targeted to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with operations expected to commence in the first quarter of 2028.

The new facility will aim to strengthen Dunham-Bush’s manufacturing capacity, serving Malaysian and international markets.

Dunham-Bush Industries managing director Yu Baoshuang said the company’s decision to locate at SPD Tech Valley was part of its next stage of expansion in Malaysia, adding that the company also saw opportunities from the growth of data centres and other high-value industries in Malaysia.

Previously, Dunham-Bush Industries established a manufacturing plant in Kajang, Selangor in 1998.

SPD Group chief executive officer Ten Wee Seong said Dunham-Bush’s decision to locate its new facility at SPD Tech Valley marked another milestone for the industrial park. “Today marks another meaningful milestone for SPD Tech Valley, and we are pleased to welcome Dunham-Bush Industries. When we first planned SPD Tech Valley, our mission was to create a smart, sustainable and managed industrial park that supports the needs of modern global industry,” said Ten in an SPA signing ceremony held at Menara Merdeka Maybank.

Meanwhile, Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the SPA reflected investor confidence in the state and the partnership between the public and private sectors.

“Today’s ceremony is more than a commercial agreement. It reflects confidence in Negeri Sembilan as an investment destination,” he said.

Ismail said the state government was targeting RM30 billion in new investments over the next five years, with a focus on investments that bring technology, expertise, quality jobs and opportunities for local vendors and supply chains.

“Our focus is not simply on capital investment. We want investments that bring technology, expertise, quality jobs and opportunities for local vendors and supply chains,” he said.

He also called on Dunham-Bush Industries to work with universities and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions to develop talent and industry skills.

“Global investors today look beyond land and cost. They consider infrastructure, connectivity, talent, utilities and the overall business ecosystem,” said Ismail.

stories.title: Chip Veteran Raises Malaysia's E&E Export Forecast to US$223 Bil
stories.summary: Malaysia’s chip industry chief raised his forecast for the nation’s electrical and electronics (E&E) exports this year to more than RM900 billion (US$223 billion), as demand fuelled by the global artificial-intelligence (AI) boom surpassed earlier expectations.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
(Aug 28): Malaysia’s chip industry chief raised his forecast for the nation’s electrical and electronics (E&E) exports this year to more than RM900 billion (US$223 billion), as demand fuelled by the global artificial-intelligence (AI) boom surpassed earlier expectations.

As recently as the second quarter, Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association president Wong Siew Hai had forecast shipments of more than RM800 billion. E&E exports rose to RM711 billion in 2025 from RM601 billion the previous year.

Malaysia’s tech exports jumped 44% in the first seven months of 2026 to about RM564 billion, accounting for roughly 48% of the country’s total shipments abroad, according to Wong. Semiconductors make up almost three-quarters of the category.

“With this momentum, it’ll probably breach RM900 billion,” this year, Wong, who spent 27 years at Intel Corp, said in an interview on Friday. “Everybody is building AI infrastructure at every level.”

The AI boom and a shift in global supply chains are driving Malaysia’s electronics exports higher. Strong demand for semiconductors, servers and data-centre equipment has boosted orders for the country’s chip industry, while companies looking to reduce their reliance on China have expanded production in Malaysia. That investment is adding capacity in assembly, testing and packaging and pushing the industry into more advanced parts of the semiconductor supply chain.
